unit.sep: Collect,organise,summarise,represent and interpret data with explicit variable/frame limits.
unit.careers: Illustrative data-recording/planning practices;no statistical or school-resource certification.
unit.phenomenon: A fictional stockreport averagesarbitrarycolourcodes and draws a time trend through unorderedcategories.
unit.drivingQuestion: Which records,summaries and graphchoices justify a useful decision? KICD: How do we use statistics in day-to-day life?
unit.storylineThread: Actualrecord → tables/types → mean → median/mode → bar → line → pie → graphaudit → actualdigitalgraphs → projectdecision → independent evidence.
unit.content: Ungrouped data; Application of graphs of data
unit.coreCompetencies:
Critical thinking and problem solving: the learner develops interpretation and inference skills when collecting data.
Digital literacy: the learner develops the skills of connecting and interacting with digital technology when using digital devices to draw graphs and charts to represent the data collected.
unit.values:
Integrity: the learner displays honesty while working in groups and collecting data such making frequency distribution tables.
Love: the learner is considerate of the other’s when working with peers to extract information from graphs and charts draw conclusions
unit.pcis: Life Skills (Decision Making): the learner makes informed decisions when identifying patterns from the graphs and charts and drawing conclusions.

sections.title: 1. Ungrouped table and summaries
sections.prompt: For FinalA,draw a value/frequencytable,totalcheck and determine mean,median and mode with evidence. Explain why an arbitrary colourcode cannot be averaged or given a meaningful median as though it were a numeric measurement.

sections.title: 2. Category bar and pie charts
sections.prompt: For FinalB,draw a labelled categorybargraph on ES12and a completepiechart on ES14. Calculate total,categoryfractions/percentages/angles and state one supported comparison. Explain why using the same dataset in these two forms does not create independent observations.

sections.title: 3. Time-ordered line graph and limits
sections.prompt: For FinalC,draw a labelled linegraph on ES13with appropriate linearscales. State overallcountchange and one limit on between-time,causal or future claims. Explain why a linejoiningunorderedcolourlabels would be different and unsupported.

sections.title: 4. A useful decision and separate actual evidence
sections.prompt: Give a modest data-basedstockdecision or follow-upquestion with a sampling/missingnesslimit. Name separateactualindividualevidence needed to confirm collection and digitalconstruction of allthreegraphforms. Explain why one classfile or these suppliedrecords cannot establish every learner performed those actions.

rubric.excellent: Complete checkedtable and allcorrectsummaries with precise numeric-versus-label reasoning.
rubric.proficient: Correct table/mean/median/mode and valid variabletype explanation.
rubric.developing: Some valid organisation/summaries but count,order,frequency or label arithmetic needs correction.
rubric.belowExpectations: Needs guided variable/table/graph/evidence questions to build a supported interpretation.

rubric.criterion: Represent category data in two graphs
rubric.excellent: Both correctlylabelledgraphs with exact completepie calculations and valid same-dataset comparison.
rubric.proficient: Correct bar/piecharts and shares/angles with a supported comparison.
rubric.developing: Some valid bars/sectors but scale,total,angles,labels or interpretation needs correction.
rubric.belowExpectations: Needs guided variable/table/graph/evidence questions to build a supported interpretation.

rubric.proficient: Correct graph/change and valid time-versus-category/evidencelimit explanation.
rubric.developing: Some valid points but scale,order,change or inference needs correction.
rubric.belowExpectations: Needs guided variable/table/graph/evidence questions to build a supported interpretation.

rubric.excellent: Specific proportionate decision/limit and precise separate collection/allthree-digital action evidence.
rubric.proficient: Useful supported decision/limit and actual-action requirements.
